result.summary: The image shows an urban intersection with marked continental crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and brick sidewalks. The environment is relatively well-equipped with basic safety features like 'No Turn On Red' signage and curb ramps, though parked cars near the crossing may limit visibility.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb line near the intersection can block the line of sight between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street, along the curb.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines.

result.summary: The image shows a residential intersection with brick townhouses and mature trees providing shade. A marked zebra crosswalk is present, supported by a traffic signal and school zone signage, though dedicated pedestrian signal heads are not clearly visible.

hazards.name: Missing Pedestrian Signal
hazards.description: While there is a vehicle traffic light, there is no visible pedestrian signal head to indicate when it is safe to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the intersection on the traffic light pole.

interventions.title: Install Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Add countdown pedestrian signals to provide clear guidance for people crossing the street and reduce uncertainty.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The image shows a narrow urban residential street with brick sidewalks and mature trees on both sides. While the narrow street geometry naturally calms traffic, the environment lacks marked pedestrian crossings and features sightline obstructions from parked vehicles.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the left side of the street may block the view between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crosswalk
hazards.description: There is no clearly marked crossing area, which may lead to unpredictable pedestrian movements and reduced driver awareness.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style crosswalk markings to clearly define the pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at crossing points to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a marked zebra crosswalk and curb ramps on a one-way residential street. Safety is hindered by the absence of pedestrian-specific signals and sightline obstructions caused by vehicles parked close to the crossing.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: A vehicle is parked very close to the crosswalk, potentially obscuring pedestrians from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the foreground sidewalk, near the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A large signpost and traffic signal pole are located in the middle of the brick sidewalk, narrowing the clear path for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Missing Pedestrian Signal
hazards.description: The intersection lacks dedicated pedestrian signals, forcing walkers to rely on vehicle signals which may not provide adequate clearance time.
